filename: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation.pdf
title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation
testbed_rationale: The three PDE datasets used from The Well benchmark suite (Rayleigh-Bénard, Turbulent Radiative Layer, and Active Matter) are publicly documented, diverse multi-scale fluid dynamics benchmarks well-suited for evaluating machine learning physics emulators.
pain_points: Compounding errors and trajectory drift in long autoregressive rollouts of chaotic dynamics
Spectral over-smoothing in deterministic regression-based PDE surrogates
High inference computational cost and latency of generative diffusion and flow matching models operating directly in pixel space
Training overhead and reduced interpretability of separately pre-trained autoencoders for latent-space generative modeling
Restriction of standard 2D discrete wavelet transforms to regular Cartesian grids, hindering immediate direct application to spherical geometry or complex domains
extraction_notes: The paper is supported by the NSF LEAP STC (Award #2019625). Datasets are sourced directly from 'The Well' benchmark dataset collection.
